primary.title: MIDI conversion for book organs and fair organs

intro.text: Play MIDI on your book or roll organ without giving up the book. Our double-valve unit sits between the key frame and the main chest, so the original operation stays completely intact. Book and MIDI can even play at the same time.

primary.title: Keep the book. Add the library.

body.text: Decap Herentals was the first to bring MIDI to the organ. Today almost every old organ is converted to MIDI, simply because it is the better way to play: it gives your organ a far wider repertoire.

Book and roll systems are what make these organs historic, and many owners are wary of changing them. Rightly so: if you convert, the organ should stay as untouched as possible. Our unit does not replace anything. The book or roll still drives the organ exactly as before. MIDI comes in alongside it, so you can play arrangements that were never punched, play live from a keyboard, or let the organ play together with other instruments.

primary.image_brief: A book organ playing with a cardboard music book running through the key frame, close-up of the book entering the key frame; 4:3

primary.title: Keep the romance of the book

body.text: When MIDI first came to the organ, many owners held back: the folding cardboard book running through the organ is part of its charm. We have an answer for that too. Our Virtual Orchestrion player projects the book fully digitally, so you watch it run while the organ plays from MIDI.

primary.image_brief: Screen showing the digital book view of Virtual Orchestrion beside a converted book organ, 4:3

items.title: Mount the units

body.text: Mount the units in the free space between key frame and main chest, in whatever orientation suits the organ.

items.image_brief: MIDI units mounted inside an open organ case near the key frame, taken with a phone torch for light; 4:3

items.title: Connect the tubing

body.text: Run a tube from the key frame to the nearest valve, and from that valve to the nearest chest input. No need to keep the notes in order.

items.image_brief: Close-up of tubes running from a key frame into a MIDI unit, hands holding a tube, 4:3

items.title: Assign the notes

body.text: Tell the included software which note each valve plays. Set the MIDI channel, and adjust note length and delay if the organ or the combination with other instruments needs it.

items.image_brief: A laptop next to the organ showing the note assignment software, screen readable, 4:3

intro.text: Because every valve can be assigned to any MIDI note, the tubing does not have to follow the scale. That keeps it short and the installation simple.

items.question: Will my organ still play its books?

answer.text: Yes. The unit sits between the key frame and the main chest and leaves the book or roll operation completely intact. Book and MIDI can play at the same time.

items.question: How many units does my organ need?

answer.text: One unit drives 16 notes. Count the keys of your organ and divide by 16, or send us the scale and we work it out for you.

items.question: Does the conversion work on roll organs and orchestrions?

answer.text: The unit is made for organs and orchestrions driven by books or piano rolls. Every conversion is made to measure for the organ, so we check each organ before we confirm it is suitable. Send us photos of the key frame and the scale.

items.question: Can the organ play together with a self-playing piano?

answer.text: Yes. The note delay of up to 500 ms lets the organ wait for piano systems that need a 500 ms pre-delay, so both play in time.
Atelier Frank Decap installs Decap MIDI units. Your own organ builder can install them too.

body.text: Send us the make, the number of keys and whether it plays books or rolls. We reply with the number of units you need and a quote.
